SRC-README.excerpt:
# 019 · Identity-Only Half-Body Portrait Dance, Six Segments (111 BPM)

![cover](./cover-saint-arms-open.png)

- **Date:** 2026-10
- **Format:** six self-contained segments, 111 BPM (beat 0.5405s / bar 2.1622s), total ≈ 73.4s
- **Input contract:** `<Picture 1>` = face crop · `<Picture 2>` = full-body appearance + environment · `<Audio 1>` = music, reused 1:1 per segment
- **Prompt:** see [prompt.md](./prompt.md)

## The problem

The performer kept opening the video by **recreating the static pose of the reference image**. H3 treats reference images as holistic truth: whatever posture the woman has in the picture leaks into frame one, and the dance only starts after a frozen "cosplay moment" of the reference. Telling the model "don't copy the pose" inside a global rule block did not survive generation.

## The breakthrough — split the two pictures down to the feature level, then demote the pose entirely

Instead of one rule block, the authority split is **written into every segment as explicit grant/deny lists**:

| Reference | Grants (preserve) | Denies (never copy) |
|---|---|---|
| `<Picture 1>` | facial identity, facial structure, eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jawline, skin, facial proportions | pose, body position, head angle, hands, arms, orientation, stance, composition — "NOT a pose / body-position / choreography / opening-frame reference" |
| `<Picture 2>` | body proportions, body scale, clothing, accessories, hair, environment, architecture, lighting direction, exposure, spatial depth, photographic realism | its exact standing posture, its use as a choreography starting pose |

And the subjective requirement "the video should feel like Picture 1's half-body portrait" is **demoted to camera/lens language only**: intimate close-up / bust / half-body / medium-close framing, a real handheld operator who may anticipate or lag, brief physical lowering for meaningful footwork. The sentence explicitly states it "does not copy the pose, head angle, hand placement, body orientation, or composition of Picture 1".

SRC-PROMPT.excerpt:
<Picture 1> is ONLY the facial identity reference for the performer.

Use <Picture 1> only to preserve:
facial identity,
facial structure,
eyes,
eyebrows,
nose,
mouth,
jawline,
skin appearance,
and recognizable facial proportions.

<Picture 1> is NOT a pose reference.
<Picture 1> is NOT a body-position reference.
<Picture 1> is NOT a choreography reference.
<Picture 1> is NOT an opening-frame reference.
Do not reproduce the head angle, hand position, arm position, body orientation, stance, or static composition of <Picture 1>.

<Picture 2> is the full-body appearance and environment reference.

Use <Picture 2> to preserve:
body proportions,
overall body scale,
clothing,
accessories,
hair as visible in the full-body reference,
environment,
architecture,
background,
lighting direction,
exposure,
spatial depth,
and realistic photographic appearance.

<Picture 2> is NOT a choreography reference.
Do not reproduce the exact standing posture shown in <Picture 2>.
Do not begin the video by copying the static pose from <Picture 2>.

There is exactly one performer.
No duplicate performer, clone, additional person, or invented background figure.

<Audio 1> is the exact audio for this segment and must be reused 1:1 as the final audio track.

Segment duration: 11.033 seconds.
Tempo: 111 BPM.
Beat: 0.5405 seconds.
Bar: 2.1622 seconds.
Phrase: 4.3243 seconds.

This is ONE continuous dance performance from the first frame to the exact audio endpoint.
The dancer never stops for a camera change, Motion Cut, portrait shot, Hero Action shot, or framing change.

Begin directly with the first choreographed movement specified below.
Do not begin from either reference image's static pose.

SRC-CAMERA.excerpt:
## CAMERA / LENS LANGUAGE

Use intimate premium portrait photography inspired by the half-body photographic distance of <Picture 1>.

This is a CAMERA / LENS LANGUAGE instruction only.
It does not copy the pose, head angle, hand placement, body orientation, or composition of <Picture 1>.

Default framing:
close-up,
bust,
half-body,
medium-close.

The performer occupies most of the available resolution.
Prioritize face, shoulders, torso, and hands.

Use a real physically operated handheld camera.
The operator may subtly anticipate the dancer, slightly lag behind the movement, or hold briefly while the dancer moves into the frame.
Do not mechanically track every limb.

When meaningful footwork occurs, physically lower or retreat slightly to reveal the active feet for a brief moment, then immediately return to the intimate half-body relationship.
Do not remain in a long full-body shot.
